title: Bindings
cards/0/body:
You could write NameBox.Text = user.Name and then copy it back. But with a dozen fields, the code turns into endless shuffling of values.

A binding links a control's property to a property of a data object. Avalonia moves the values back and forth for you.
cards/1/body: Every element has a DataContext: an object with data. If it is not set, the element takes its parent's. Usually you set it on the window, and every element inside sees the same view model.
cards/2/task: Everything is already set up. Type a name into the TextBox and watch it reach the model and come back in the greeting.
cards/3/q: The window has DataContext = new MainViewModel(). What is the DataContext of a TextBox inside the window if you do not set it?
cards/3/options/0: The same MainViewModel, inherited from the parent
cards/3/explain: DataContext flows down the tree until someone overrides it.
cards/4/task: Now change the name from code and check whether the screen updated.
cards/5/q: Bind the text to the Title property
cards/5/explain: The binding path is the name of a property on the DataContext.
cards/6/q: What is true about bindings? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/0: A binding looks up the property on the DataContext
cards/6/options/1: DataContext is inherited from the parent
cards/6/options/2: Bindings spare you from copying values by hand
cards/6/explain: You can bind any property: numbers, flags, collections, colors.
cards/7/q: Match each term to its meaning
cards/7/pairs/0/1: The data object for an element
cards/7/pairs/1/1: A link to the Name property
cards/7/pairs/3/1: A class holding the window's data
